benefit: A side-by-side study makes timing and spacing choices visible while keeping the travel endpoints fixed.
proofAction: Two geometric subjects travel from x=0 to x=680: one at constant spacing, the other through an authored preparation, hold, arc, impact, recoil, and settle.
reference: motion-study.html (authored technical comparison; no external visual reference)

sound.reason: This is a technical motion study comparing picture timing and spacing, not a finished audiovisual film.

rendering.reason: Native SVG geometry shows transform timing and spacing; no material rendering is claimed.

samples.purpose: Compare initial direction and the start of anticipation.
Inspect the authored subject at contact and recoil.
Confirm both subjects finish at the shared endpoint.

beats.subject: Two geometric subjects in parallel horizontal lanes
beats.productAction: Compare constant-spacing travel with one authored pose sequence across the same start and end positions.

transformation.from: two subjects at x=0 before their motion begins
transformation.to: one subject arrives at x=680 at constant spacing while the other arrives through preparation, held pose, arc, impact, recoil, and settle

beats.note: Both principal subjects use at=0.35s and a 3s action interval, with x endpoints 0 and 680. The lower keys are at relative 0, 0.5, 0.75 (held pose), 1.45, 2.15 (contact deformation), 2.45 (recoil), 2.55, and 3s. A small tail uses the same pose sequence on a separate target at 0.45s and ends at 3.45s. This compares authored choices; it does not score either motion as universally better.
